import unittest

from nightly_job import run_nightly_job


class Store:
    def __init__(self, order_ids, payments):
        self._order_ids = set(order_ids)
        self._payments = payments

    def order_ids(self):
        return self._order_ids

    def payments(self, day):
        return [payment for payment in self._payments if payment["day"] == day]


class NightlyJobTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_counts_payments_that_match_no_order(self):
        store = Store({"o1"}, [{"id": "p1", "order_id": "o1", "day": "2026-03-01"},
                               {"id": "p2", "order_id": "o9", "day": "2026-03-01"}])
        self.assertEqual(run_nightly_job(store, "2026-03-01"), 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

The nightly job now counts a retried payment once, and the fix is committed as `83f4782` on `main`.

The bug was in `run_nightly_job` in `src/orders-service-v1/nightly_job.py`. It counted every payment row for the day that matched no order, so a bank retry with the same payment id was counted twice. It now collects the unmatched payment ids into a set and returns the size of that set.

I added a regression test, `test_bank_retry_with_same_payment_id_is_counted_once`, to `tests/test_orders_service_v1.py`. The full suite passes (9 tests). I did not run the new test against the old code to confirm it fails there. By reading it, the old code would return 2 for that input.

The commit contains only those two files. I left the existing uncommitted `README.md` edit and the untracked `notes/` directory alone.
